title: What is Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) & How It Differs from Scheme-I
content: The Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS), designated as Scheme-II under the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations 2018, is a self-declaration of conformity framework primarily applicable to notified electronic and IT goods. Key differences from Scheme-I (ISI Mark) include: 1) Factory Audit: Under CRS, no preliminary factory audit is conducted prior to grant of registration; 2) Testing: Registration is granted on the basis of a test report from a BIS-recognized laboratory located in India; 3) Standard Mark: Products bear the CRS Registration Mark with the statement 'Self Declaration - Conforming to IS XXXXX' and a unique R-number (e.g. R-XXXXXXXX) instead of the ISI mark.

title: Which Product Categories Fall Under Compulsory Registration (CRS)
content: Electronic, IT, and consumer electrical goods are notified under the Compulsory Registration Scheme by MeitY, MNRE, and Ministry of Power. Major notified categories include: 1) IT Goods: Laptops, notebooks, tablets, servers, printers, and scanners; 2) Audio/Visual & Electronics: Television sets, LED monitors, Bluetooth wireless speakers, and smartwatches; 3) Power & Accessories: Power adapters, mobile phone chargers, power banks, and UPS/inverters; 4) Lighting: Self-ballasted LED lamps (IS 16102-1) and LED drivers; 5) Solar Products: Solar PV modules and grid-connected inverters.

title: The Step-by-Step Registration Process for CRS Products
content: The registration process under CRS follows an online workflow: 1) Sample Testing: The manufacturer sends product samples to a BIS-recognized laboratory in India for testing against the relevant Indian Standard; 2) Test Report Generation: The laboratory uploads the verified test report directly to the BIS CRS portal (the report is valid for application submission for 90 days); 3) Online Application: The manufacturer or Authorized Indian Representative (AIR for foreign manufacturers) submits the application on crsbis.in with product documentation and fee; 4) Grant of Registration: BIS evaluates the application and issues the Registration Number (R-XXXXXXXX).

title: Standard Mark and Labeling Requirements for CRS Registered Products
content: All products registered under CRS must display the standard Registration Mark on the product body and packaging before market release. The mark must clearly display: 1) The standard statement: 'Self Declaration - Conforming to IS XXXXX (Part X)', 2) The unique BIS Registration Number assigned to the manufacturing location (e.g. 'R-XXXXXXXX'), and 3) The official CRS logo. The mark must be legible, indelible, and placed prominently on the rating label.
